question: How does the text conclude the division of the path of space at the highest level?
premises: Śāntyatītā is said to consist of eighteen worlds.
Śāntyatītā is also described as itself a world.
The division of the path of space is declared taught as instructed by revered Śambhu.
inference: The path of space culminates in Śāntyatītā and is formally concluded as an authoritative teaching of Śambhu.
uncertainties: The relation between eighteen worlds and Śāntyatītā being itself a world is compactly stated and may reflect a doctrinal distinction.
plain_english: Śāntyatītā consists of eighteen worlds, yet it is also itself a world. Thus the division of the path of space has been told, as instructed by revered Śambhu.
